policy.psdImportNote: The browser editor does not parse PSD/KRA directly. Export selected layers to transparent PNGs that retain one exact full-canvas size; do not include third-party art files in the public repository and respect each source's terms.

sources.name: See-through — Single-image Layer Decomposition for Anime Characters
sources.author: shitagaki-lab and paper authors
sources.notes: Research tool can decompose one anime illustration into up to 23 semantic layers (including hair, face, eyes, clothing and accessories), with inpainting and inferred draw order. Official README says default inference needs about 12–16 GB GPU VRAM at 1280 resolution; 4-bit quantized inference uses about 8 GB VRAM, and training used 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. This is not compatible with a 2 GB memory budget as the core editor; evaluate only as an optional off-device/preparation pipeline for artwork the user owns or is permitted to modify. Code license does not automatically determine model-weight, dependency, input-art or training-data rights.
sources.modelMemoryNote: Reported GPU VRAM: 12–16 GB default, ~8 GB quantized at 1280 resolution. This is VRAM, not system RAM; no 2 GB system-RAM claim is made.

sources.name: Stretchy Studio

sources.modelMemoryNote: No low-memory profile verified. Do not place it in the critical 2 GB runtime path without benchmarking.

sources.name: Anime Avatar — configurable procedural anime avatar
sources.author: konard
sources.notes: Repository describes modular 2D SVG components for face, eyes, hair, body, legs and background, with configurable detail levels. Study the component boundaries and procedural rendering approach as an alternative when licensed part packs cannot fill a slot. This is a code/reference candidate, not an external modular sprite archive; do not assume separate reference images, 3D models or dependencies share the code license.
sources.modelMemoryNote: The SVG route is more aligned with low-memory rendering than embedding a diffusion model; 3D mode and full app dependencies are not part of the 2 GB target until measured.
